'''''Why Johnny Can't Add: The Failure of the New Math''''' is a 1973 book by [[Morris Kline]], in which the author severely criticized the teaching practices characteristic of the "[[New Math]]" fashion for school teaching, which were based on [[Nicolas Bourbaki|Bourbaki]]'s approach to mathematical research and [[mathematics education in the United States]].<ref>{{cite book|author1=Jürgen Maass|author2=Wolfgang Schlöglmann|title=New Mathematics Education Research and Practice|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Js8NX11zL7QC&pg=PA1|year=2006|publisher=Sense Publishers|isbn=978-90-77874-74-5|page=1}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|author1=[[Joseph W. Dauben]]|author2=[[Christoph J. Scriba]]|title=Writing the History of Mathematics: Its Historical Development|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=oXjMYIonXTYC&pg=PA458|date=23 September 2002|publisher=Springer Science & Business Media|isbn=978-3-7643-6167-9|page=458}}</ref> Reactions were immediate, and the book became a best seller in its genre and was translated into many languages.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Fey |first=James T. |date=1978 |title=Change in mathematics education since the late 1950's - ideas and realisation U.S.A. |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/3481942 |journal=Educational Studies in Mathematics |volume=9 |issue=3 |pages=339–353 |issn=0013-1954}}</ref>
